caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 467 of 1996.
lawyer:
B Hossain, Deputy Attorney-General instructed by Mvi Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record------For the Petitioners. 
Firoj Shah, Advocate-on-Record------For Respondent No.1. 
Not represented------Respondent No.2.
parties:
Government of Bangladesh and others  ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md Hafizur Rahman and another ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mainor Reza Chowdhury J: This petition for leave to appeal is against the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition, No. 1093 of 1989 making the Rule absolute and declaring that the order of the Court of Settlement and the enlistment of the case holding in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings to be illegal and without any lawful authority. 

 2. The facts are that, the respondents (petitioners in the writ petition) challenged inclusion of holding No. 15/B, Block-B, Second Colony, Mirpur, Dhaka in the 'Kha' list of abandoned buildings before the Court of Settlement. The case of the respondents was that the case holding originally belonged to one Md Shamsuddin who got the same as per lease agreement of 1953. He possessed the same for 12 years and thereafter executed a deed of agreement for sale on 11 December 1970 in favour of one Sayeda Reba Habib for consideration of Taka 20,000.00 as earnest money before executing and registering the sale deed. The said Md Shamsuddin died on 20-2-73 leaving behind his mother and two full brothers as his heirs. In Succession Case No. 377 of 1980 Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka issued succession certificate in favour of his heirs mother Mossammat Sharifan Bibi and two full brothers Md Zafar Mia and Md Zakir Mia. The heirs of Md Shams uddin received the balance consideration of Taka 10,000.00 from the said purchaser Sayeda Reba Habib and they executed and registered a sale deed in her favour on 26-5-1980 in respect of the said holding. Thereafter, Sayeda Reba, Habib while in possession sold 2.5 kattas of the said plot to respondent No. 1 for Taka 50,000.00 and the other 2.5 kattas of the said holding to respondent No. 2 for a consideration of Taka 50,000.00 by sale deed dated the 30-1-81 who have been in possession since their purchase. The names of the respondents were mutated in Mutation Case No. 9193 (m) 81 dated 27-5-81 and they obtained duplicate carbon receipt. They also paid rent to the Government Tahsil Kachari in their own names for the year 1392 BS in respect of the case holding and obtained rent receipt No. A-835956 dated 8-1-86. There was also an inquiry in respect of the case holding pursuant to Memo No. Miscellaneous 59/85/3686/1 dated 18-6-85 of the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement, Ministry of Works, Segunbagicha and it was reported that the respondent No. 2 has been possessing their respective portion of land of the holding on the basis of sale deed dated 30-1-81. It was also reported that on the death of the original allottee Md Shamsuddin his aforementioned heirs sold the said land by sale deed No. 3360 dated 26-5-1980 to Sayeda Reba Habib who again sold the said plot to the petitioners by sale deed dated 30-1-81. 

 3. The Chairman, Court of Settlement by order dated 10-5-89 dismissed the case as no one appeared on repeated calls when the case was taken up for hearing. Being aggrieved the respondents filed Writ Petition against the order of the Court of Settlement. It was submitted before the High Court Division that neither the vendor of the respondents nor her predecessor left the country. The petitioners are Bangladesh nationals and have been in exclusive possession of the case holding and their enlistment in the 'Kha' list of the abandoned buildings has no basis. It was further submitted that the Court of Settlement failed to exercise its duty as a Court of Settlement to ascertain if the case holding is in fact, abandoned property or not and if the petitioner have been in possession of the case building on the basis of their titled deeds. It was also submitted that on the date of hearing the petitioners could not appear before the Court of Settlement as admittedly no notice was served upon them. It was found by the High Court Division that the Court of Settlement had not been constituted when the respondents filed application before that Court. It was subsequently constituted and their petition was considered in their absence without serving any notice on them. It was found that the address of the respondents were in the record and yet no notice was served upon them. It was explained that the Court of Settlement was constituted after a long gap and they had no knowledge of the date of hearing and therefore could not appear on the date of the hearing. The submission was found to have substance by the High Court Division. The High Court Division also found from the record that the original allottee Md Shamsuddin entered into an agreement on 11-12-1970 in favour of Sayeda Reba Habib and received part of the consideration money. After his death, his heirs received the balance money and executed sale deed in favour of Sayeda Reba Habib who subsequently transferred the case holding in favour of the respondents who have been in possession since then. It was also found that the heirs of Sayeda Reba Habib had taken our succession certificate the respondents had been in possession and paid rent. 

 4. It is found that the Court of Settlement did not dispose of the application on merit which it is required to do under the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 and instead dismissed the application as the respondents were not present in the Court. By not deciding the case on merit the Court of Settlement acted illegally and without lawful authority. However, we find that the High Court Division found from the record that the case holding was not an abandoned building. The petitioner have failed to show any illegality in the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in the writ petition.
